name: Tilion

modes.label: Managed browser service
modes.note: No CPU/RAM per session published. Two conflicting official figures: blog (2026-08-07) says '$0.03 per browser-hour' pay-per-use with free credits of 'a few hundred hours'; current pricing page shows subscription plans (Free/Developer $19.99/Pro $99.99/Scale $499) with included browser hours and 'Overage billed per hour' at an unpublished rate. Effective included-hour cost: Developer $0.20/h, Pro $0.20/h, Scale ~$0.10/h.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: 10 browser h/mo, 500 MB egress/mo, 100 sessions/mo; hard stop at allowance (no overage).

plans.name: Developer
plans.note: 100 browser h/mo + 2 GB egress/mo included; unlimited sessions; overage billed per hour (rate unpublished).

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: 500 browser h/mo + 10 GB egress/mo included; unlimited sessions; overage billed per hour (rate unpublished).

plans.name: Scale
plans.note: 5,000 browser h/mo + 35 GB egress/mo included; unlimited sessions; overage billed per hour (rate unpublished).

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: 250+ concurrent sessions, unlimited hours and egress, invoiced billing, engineer support channel. Price not published.

features.ip_note: Tilion Cloud (closed beta 2026-07-14, public/self-serve since 2026-08-07 per blog) advertises residential IP egress; plan egress allowances 500 MB (Free) to 35 GB/mo (Scale), Enterprise unlimited; no per-GB overage or residential price published; self-run Fortress engine uses whatever IP/proxy you bring.

caveats: Browser infrastructure: concurrency tiers and runtime-overage billing advertised; verify full duration/overage details in raw evidence. CPU/RAM allocation not documented.
No invented browser vCPU or memory allocation: normalized 4/8 rate remains null. Proxy traffic is not necessarily equivalent to sandbox egress.
Free includes 10h/500MB/100 sessions; Developer 100h/2GB, Pro 500h/10GB, Scale 5000h/35GB. Numeric overage rate not on captured page; plans say contact us.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Re-checked 2026-09-28 at https://tilion.com/pricing: plans Free $0 (3 concurrent, 10 browser h, 500 MB egress, stops at allowance), Developer $19.99 (15, 100 h, 2 GB), Pro $99.99 (50, 500 h, 10 GB), Scale $499 (200, 5,000 h, 35 GB), Enterprise custom. Overage is "billed per hour" but no numeric overage rate is published, and no CPU/RAM per session: still unpriceable beyond the included hours.

fleet.tiers: Free 3; Developer 15; Pro 50; Scale 200; Enterprise 250+ custom.
fleet.notes: Every pricing-tier CTA is 'Contact us' (mailto team@tilion.dev, subject 'Tilion access'), yet the 2026-08-07 blog says 'No waitlist, no sales call' and dashboard.tilion.dev offers 'Create an account'. Concurrency: Free 3, Developer 15, Pro 50, Scale 200, Enterprise 250+. Verification/activation time unknown.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Each session gets its own browser, destroyed on release, and no cookies, profile, or disk state is ever carried between sessions or between customers.
snapshot_auto.note: Tilion Cloud sessions are ephemeral browsers; 'persistent' mode only means the session lives until ttl/idle_timeout and keeps cookies across calls within that session.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A session is one isolated browser, dedicated to you for its lifetime and destroyed on release. No cookies, profile, or disk state is ever reused between sessions.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/profile-save API in the Cloud docs. The self-run open-source Fortress MCP server has get_cookies/save_profile/load_profile ('persist or restore an authenticated session'), which is a browser profile on your own machine, not a machine snapshot.

own_agent_api.quote: State a goal in natural language against a domain. Tilion replays a cached skill when it has one and derives a new one when it does not, so repeat calls get cheaper.
own_agent_api.note: Only the provider's own browser agent: POST /v1/task (NL goal -> REPLAY/DERIVE/HEAL a skill on a session), plus named agent tasks (POST /v1/agent) and templates; async jobs polled. No streaming events, follow-ups or conversations; no Claude Code/Codex/etc. Borderline for the definition.

ingress_rules.quote: The token expires in 300 seconds and is scoped to this session. Mint one immediately before you attach; do not cache it.
ingress_rules.note: Browser is reachable only via tokenized CDP connect_url (raw CDP can be disabled per key: 'returns 403 if raw CDP is not enabled for your key') and short-lived session-scoped live-view/VNC tokens. No arbitrary ports or IP allowlists.

image_oci.quote: POST /v1/session accepts an empty body, and every field below is optional. The defaults give you an ephemeral, headless browser in the nearest region.
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Session config fields (mode, region, residential, full_browser, block_ads, ttl, idle_timeout, persona, proxy_rotation, warm_up) are the whole surface; there is no custom-image/OCI option, since the product only ever launches its own Chromium build.

docker_inside.quote: Tilion provides isolated cloud browsers over a REST API. Create a browser with one call, drive it over CDP, and pay only while it runs.
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The product exposes only a browser (CDP/REST), with no general-purpose compute or container runtime inside the session.

nested_virt.quote: Tilion provides isolated cloud browsers over a REST API.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. A managed browser session exposes no /dev/kvm or general OS access.

desktop.quote: The whole Chrome window (tabs, omnibox), interactive, off a warm pool. false gives the lighter JPEG page-screencast
desktop.note: full_browser sessions expose a real, viewable/interactive desktop via VNC (live_view_url / vnc-token / vnc-ws), i.e. a headful Chrome window, not just a screencast.

computer_use.quote: The act tools drive the page the session is currently on. They target elements by CSS selector or, for click, by visible text.
computer_use.note: MCP/REST act tools (fill, type_text, click, press_key, scroll, set_clipboard via POST /v1/session/{id}/act) let an agent act on the live page while watching the live view; this is DOM/selector-driven action rather than screenshot-coordinate clicking, but functions as the product's computer-use style control surface.

captcha_solving.quote: Is Fortress undetectable? No, and it does not claim to be. ... Anti-bot systems also weigh the egress IP and behavior, so a datacenter IP still gets blocked on the hardest targets regardless of fingerprint.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Tilion focuses on fingerprint-level stealth (Fortress engine) and residential egress/IP rotation to avoid triggering bot defenses; there is no built-in CAPTCHA-solving API/service documented (the FAQ mentions clearing a Turnstile challenge as a detection test, not a solving feature).

ssh.quote: Tilion provides isolated cloud browsers over a REST API. Create a browser with one call, drive it over CDP, and pay only while it runs.
ssh.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Access is via REST/CDP/MCP and a VNC live view only; no SSH endpoint is documented.

snapshot.quote: A session is one isolated browser, dedicated to you for its lifetime and destroyed on release. No cookies, profile, or disk state is ever reused between sessions.
snapshot.note: Sessions are ephemeral or persistent (in-memory, cookie state kept only for the session's own lifetime); no filesystem or memory snapshot/restore mechanism is documented.

fork.quote: A session is one isolated browser, dedicated to you for its lifetime and destroyed on release. No cookies, profile, or disk state is ever reused between sessions.
fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No clone/fork-session endpoint is documented; each session starts from a clean state.

fork_running.quote: A session is one isolated browser, dedicated to you for its lifetime and destroyed on release.
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (no fork capability at all, see `fork`).

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: A session is one isolated browser, dedicated to you for its lifetime and destroyed on release.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (no fork/snapshot capability at all).

pause_resume.quote: Always release in a finally block. Sessions bill until released.
pause_resume.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Sessions are either running (billing) or released/dead; there is no pause/suspend-and-resume-later state, only mode=ephemeral/persistent with ttl and idle_timeout.

wake_on_request.quote: starting: Browser is booting. connect_url may not work yet. ready: Attachable and drivable. closing: Release in progress. dead: Ended. Create a new session.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. A dead/released session cannot be woken; a new session must be created (though warm pools make that fast, e.g. ~718ms per the Tilion Cloud blog).

persistent_disk.quote: A session is one isolated browser, dedicated to you for its lifetime and destroyed on release. No cookies, profile, or disk state is ever reused between sessions.
persistent_disk.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Explicitly no disk state carried across sessions; nothing persists past release.

volume_attach.quote: POST /v1/session accepts an empty body, and every field below is optional.
volume_attach.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No volume/storage-attach option exists among session configuration fields.

volume_shared.quote: POST /v1/session accepts an empty body, and every field below is optional.
volume_shared.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (no volumes at all, see volume_attach).

auto_stop_idle.quote: idle_timeout | number (s) | plan default | Reclaimed after this long idle
auto_stop_idle.note: Sessions are automatically reclaimed after idle_timeout seconds of inactivity.

live_resize.quote: POST /v1/session accepts an empty body, and every field below is optional. The defaults give you an ephemeral, headless browser in the nearest region.
live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No CPU/RAM sizing is exposed at all (sessions are just 'a browser'), so there is nothing to live-resize.

agent_harnesses.quote: Every plan runs the same browser. The tier sets concurrency and how many hours you get
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Tilion ships its own browser-automation MCP server and REST 'agent tasks'/'skills'/'templates' for browser workflows, but does not offer or preinstall third-party coding-agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) inside sessions.

harness_api.quote: State a goal in natural language against a domain. Tilion replays a cached skill when it has one and derives a new one when it does not, so repeat calls get cheaper.
harness_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. This is a first-party API for Tilion's own browser task/skill agent, not an API to drive a third-party coding harness inside the sandbox.

lang_python.quote: Your existing tooling works unchanged. Playwright, Puppeteer, chromedp, and raw WebSockets all attach the same way, so there is no Tilion SDK to learn and no rewrite: point connectOverCDP at the URL and your existing script runs.
lang_python.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Tilion is a browser-only session (REST/CDP/MCP); it explicitly has no SDK of its own, and there is no general-purpose Python code-execution runtime inside the machine.

lang_node.quote: Your existing tooling works unchanged. Playwright, Puppeteer, chromedp, and raw WebSockets all attach the same way, so there is no Tilion SDK to learn and no rewrite: point connectOverCDP at the URL and your existing script runs.
lang_node.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Node/Playwright is used as a *client* driving the remote browser over CDP from the caller's own machine; there is no Node runtime executing inside the Tilion session itself.

public_ipv4.quote: Set residential: true on session create to route the session's traffic through residential IPs. Residential egress needs a paid plan.
public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Tilion exposes egress IP options (datacenter default, residential on paid plans) for outbound browser traffic; there is no dedicated public IPv4 assigned per machine for inbound access, since sessions are reached only via tokenized CDP/VNC/live-view URLs, not raw ports.

inbound_https.quote: The endpoint returns 403 if raw CDP is not enabled for your key, and 409 if the session has no live browser.
inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. There is no concept of exposing an arbitrary HTTPS port on the session; the only exposed endpoints are the provider's own tokenized CDP/live-view/VNC URLs, not user-run services on the machine.

egress_allowlist.quote: The proxy_rotation field on session create controls when the egress IP changes: per_request, per_session, manual.
egress_allowlist.note: Documented network controls are about which egress IP/rotation policy is used (datacenter vs residential, rotation cadence), not allow/deny-list or no-internet egress restrictions; no such control is documented.

egress_http_rules.quote: POST /v1/session accepts an empty body, and every field below is optional.
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No HTTP method/path-level egress rule control is documented; the only egress option is residential/datacenter IP choice.

guest_firewall.quote: Tilion provides isolated cloud browsers over a REST API.
guest_firewall.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Sessions are single-purpose Chromium browsers with no root shell or general OS access, so there is no nftables/iptables surface inside the guest.

secret_proxy.quote: Text you pass to fill, type_text, and set_clipboard, such as passwords and tokens, is never logged or echoed back.
secret_proxy.note: Tilion avoids logging/echoing secrets typed into the browser (fill/type_text/set_clipboard) and suggests users paste passwords in the live view themselves, but there is no first-party HTTP credential-injection proxy for arbitrary APIs; secrets are only ever entered as page input, not injected as headers.

gpu.quote: Every plan runs the same browser. The tier sets concurrency and how many hours you get
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. A managed-browser product with no GPU machine tier documented anywhere on pricing/docs.

windows.quote: Tilion provides isolated cloud browsers over a REST API. Create a browser with one call, drive it over CDP, and pay only while it runs.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The hosted product runs Chromium sessions on Tilion's own Linux-based cloud infrastructure; no Windows machine option is offered (Fortress the open-source engine can be built on Windows locally, but that's not the Cloud product).

macos.quote: Tilion provides isolated cloud browsers over a REST API. Create a browser with one call, drive it over CDP, and pay only while it runs.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No macOS machine option is offered by the hosted Cloud product.

byoc.quote: Enterprise 250 concurrent sessions and up, unlimited hours and egress, invoiced billing, and a support channel with the engineers who run the fleet.
byoc.note: Even the Enterprise tier is described as a support channel with the team that runs Tilion's own fleet, not a deployment into the customer's cloud account; no BYOC offering is documented.

static_egress_ip.quote: The proxy_rotation field on session create controls when the egress IP changes: per_request ... per_session ... manual — The IP changes only when you ask.
static_egress_ip.note: Proxies page documents residential egress and three rotation policies (including 'manual', which keeps one IP until you request a change) but there is no 'static' or 'dedicated' IP offering, and no fixed IP survives past a session's lifetime. No mention of a persistent/fixed outbound IP anywhere in docs or pricing.

arm64.quote: Tilion creates an isolated browser for you over a REST call. You drive it with the tools you already use and pay only while it runs.
arm64.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Tilion Cloud is a managed browser-session API (create session -> connect over CDP -> release); there is no VM/instance-type or CPU-architecture selection surfaced anywhere in the API (session configuration only exposes mode, region, residential, full_browser, block_ads, ttl, idle_timeout, persona, proxy_rotation).

max_session_h.quote: Max session length | 30 min | 2 h | 6 h | 12 h
max_session_h.note: Max session length is tiered: Free 30 min, Developer 2 h, Pro 6 h, Scale 12 h; 'Enterprise plans lift every cap' with no published number. Value given is the highest documented self-serve cap (Scale plan, 12 h).
